A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched across additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffusion reward fine-tuning and MNIST noise-scheduling experiments in Section 6, Tables 1–2 and appendix image comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds HPSv2 reward fine-tuning results in Table 2 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The written sampling specification changes locally: reverse and guided SDEs (6) and (8) revise the time/drift convention and add the noise-schedule factor q(t) multiplying the score. Algorithms reference these equations, but the bilevel update rules and gradient estimators remain unchanged; implementation changes are not established.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains text-to-image reward fine-tuning and MNIST image generation. HPSv2 is introduced as another reward function within the retained fine-tuning task, without a documented new dataset or distinct population.

E2.justification: Fine-tuning retains grid search, random search, Bayesian search and weighted sum, including in the added HPSv2 comparison. Noise scheduling retains the same search methods and default DDIM comparator.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 adds a fine-tuning condition using HPSv2 instead of the synthetic ResNet-18 reward, retaining FID, CLIP and runtime evaluation with gamma = 1000. The previously reported experimental settings and Appendix F procedures are otherwise unchanged.

E4.justification: The added HPSv2 comparison explicitly tests robustness to the lower-level reward choice, supported by Table 2 and an elephant-image comparison in Figure 5. Existing scheduler analyses and appendix cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose four fine-tuning repetitions and Bayesian-search random_state = 42 in Appendix F.1. The new table follows the existing ± reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports HPSv2 results, including bilevel FID 137.23 ± 1.7 and CLIP 37.10 ± 3.2, alongside comparator results. Original Table 1, the noise-scheduling table renumbered from 2 to 3, and appendix image scores are unchanged. The added scores concern a different reward condition, not a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 revises reverse-diffusion Equations (6) and (8), including score scaling and reverse-time specification. Appendix C changes the noise distribution following Equation (23) from N(mu_t, sigma_t² I_d) to N(0, I_d). The principal assumptions, proposition, theorem and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a diffusion-friendly first-order bilevel framework, inference-only reward fine-tuning, noise-scheduler optimization and advantages over hyperparameter-search baselines. The additional experiment supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 now interprets the HPSv2 comparison as evidence of robustness across lower-level rewards and extends its image-quality discussion to preservation of elephant anatomy. The theoretical applicability discussion and existing qualifications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a paper-specific code-release statement and repository link, absent from v1. Hardware, batch sizes, search ranges, warm-start settings and EMA documentation in Appendix F are retained. Repository availability is reported by the PDF, not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds works including HPSv2, variational diffusion models, simple diffusion and learned adaptive noise. Section 7 distinguishes likelihood-based scheduler learning from directly optimizing sample quality through bilevel optimization. Updated Shen publication entries represent retained works rather than new citations.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits, added HPSv2 and related-work paragraphs, and updated affiliations and publication information. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain intact, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figure 5, clarifies the synthetic-reward caption of Table 1, and corrects Figure 1's KL argument order to match the existing objective. Retained tables, plots and appendix galleries are renumbered or repositioned within the same overall layout.

improvement.justification: The HPSv2 experiment adds useful support beyond v1's synthetic-reward fine-tuning evidence. The code-release information, localized mathematical and diagram corrections, and clearer comparison with prior scheduler learning also improve documentation and consistency. These gains are incremental: the principal theory, existing results and overall task coverage remain largely unchanged.
